script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. July 28th already.
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。もう7月28日ですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning, Alex. It really is. Another warm one, isn't it?
script.ja: アレックス、おはよう。本当に。また暑くなりそうだね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, mainly clear, 33.5 degrees Celsius high. But then it says 55% rain probability.
script.ja: ええ、主に晴れで最高33.5度。でも、降水確率55％って書いてありますね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's just how July is sometimes. Always a chance of a sudden shower.
script.ja: 7月はそういうものよ。突然の通り雨があるかもしれない。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I guess. I jump at everything these days. Pretty sure it's the baby. My little one was up twice last night, trying to climb out of the crib.
script.ja: そうですね。最近、何にでもびっくりしちゃって。多分、うちの子のせいです。昨夜も2回起きて、ベビーベッドからよじ登ろうとしていました。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They start moving fast at that age.
script.ja: その年頃になると、動きが早くなるのよね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I need my coffee. Anyway, welcome to The Daily Tanu-chan Show. Hope everyone's having a good morning.
script.ja: コーヒーが必要です。さて、皆さん、『The Daily Tanu-chan Show』へようこそ。良い朝をお過ごしください。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I'm on my second cup of tea. Ready for the news?
script.ja: 私は紅茶2杯目よ。ニュースの準備はいい？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Always. First up, the government plans to raise the bar for permanent residency. Higher income, certain Japanese language level...
script.ja: いつでも。まず、政府は永住権の基準を厳しくする予定だそうです。より高い収入、一定の日本語レベル...

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a big change for many people. It's a challenging time.
script.ja: 多くの人にとって大きな変化ね。大変な時期だわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I mean, it just feels like this whole issue is pretty *intractable*.
script.ja: ええ、なんていうか、この問題全体がかなり『intractable』な気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Intractable? It's a problem that's really difficult to deal with or solve.
script.ja: Intractable？それは、対処したり解決したりするのが本当に難しい問題のことね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right. That's what I mean. Not going to change at my office, I guess.
script.ja: そう、それです。うちの会社では変わらないでしょうけどね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Next, a foreign hiker on Mount Fuji lost consciousness and died, the second fatality this climbing season.
script.ja: 次は、富士山で外国人登山者が意識を失って死亡したとのこと。今シーズンの死者は2人目だそうよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, that's terrible. I feel like I read about things like this on Mount Fuji every year. It's almost... *obsessive* how often it happens.
script.ja: ああ、それはひどいですね。富士山のこういうニュース、毎年読んでいる気がします。こんなに頻繁に起こるなんて、まるで『obsessive』ですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Obsessive means you can't stop thinking about something. I think you mean it's a recurring issue, or a persistent problem.
script.ja: Obsessiveは、あることについて考えるのを止められないという意味よ。あなたが言いたいのは、繰り返される問題、あるいは根強い問題ということかしら。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, right. Recurring. Yeah. It's dangerous, I guess.
script.ja: ああ、そうか。繰り返される。ええ。危険なんですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. People underestimate it.
script.ja: そうよ。みんな、富士山を甘く見ているわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: And finally, a simple kanji character has five different pronunciations depending on the sentence. Five!
script.ja: そして最後に、一つの簡単な漢字が、文脈によって5つの異なる発音を持つというニュースです。5つですよ！

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's one of those things that makes Japanese unique. Not always easy.
script.ja: 日本語がユニークな理由の一つね。いつも簡単ではないわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: My head hurts just thinking about it. No wonder foreign learners struggle.
script.ja: 考えただけで頭が痛くなります。外国の学習者が苦労するのも無理ないですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, but they get there.
script.ja: ええ、でも彼らはできるようになるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, hey, speaking of unique things, do you know what today is? My phone says it's 'Amateur Radio Day' in Japan.
script.ja: ああ、そういえば、ユニークな話で、今日が何の日か知っていますか？私の携帯には、日本では「アマチュア無線の日」と出ています。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's right. It marks the day in 1952 when amateur radio got its first preliminary license after the war.
script.ja: そうね。1952年に戦後初めてアマチュア無線の予備免許が発行された日を記念して制定されたのよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I didn't know that. So, like, people just talk to strangers from far away on the radio?
script.ja: へえ、それは知りませんでした。じゃあ、ラジオで遠くの見知らぬ人と話す感じですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Exactly. They connect with people all over the world, using specific radio frequencies. It's a hobby.
script.ja: その通りよ。特定の無線周波数を使って、世界中の人々と繋がるの。趣味ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Huh. That's kind of amazing, actually. Maybe I should get into that. I could talk to people while the baby's sleeping.
script.ja: へえ。それって実はちょっとすごいですね。私も始めてみようかな。赤ちゃんが寝ている間に、誰かと話せるかも。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You'd need a license.
script.ja: 免許が必要になるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh. Right. Anyway, my morning walk was lovely today, by the way. The air felt a little lighter than yesterday.
script.ja: ああ。そうか。ところで、今朝の散歩は素晴らしかったわ。昨日に比べて少し空気が軽かった気がする。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Oh, that's nice. Mine was just a dash to the coffee machine.
script.ja: ああ、それはいいですね。私はただコーヒーマシンに駆け込んだだけです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Well, enjoy your coffee, Alex. We'll be back tomorrow.
script.ja: じゃあ、コーヒーを楽しんで、アレックス。また明日ね。
